item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
961
ABPZ20 KNHC 280519
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Thu Aug 27 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Karina, located well south-southwest of the southern tip of
the Baja California Peninsula, on Tropical Storm Lowell, located
well east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands, and on Tropical Storm
Lala, located several hundred miles north of Kure Atoll.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form this weekend well to the
south of southwestern Mexico. Environmental conditions appear
favorable for gradual development of this system, and a tropical
depression is likely to form early next week while it moves
west-northwestward to northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands in a few days. Some gradual development is possible
thereafter and a tropical depression could form during the middle
part of next week while the system moves slowly west-northwestward,
well offshore of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Karina are issued under WMO
header WTPZ31 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP1.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Karina are issued under WMO
header WTPZ21 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP1.

header WTPZ32 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP2.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Lowell are issued under WMO

OF THE COAST OF SOUTHWEST MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM MST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...12.7N 114.3W
ABOUT 760 MI...1225 KM SSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 13 MPH...20 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...999 MB...29.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Karina was
located near latitude 12.7 North, longitude 114.3 West. Karina is
moving toward the northwest near 13 mph (20 km/h) and this
general motion is expected to continue over the next couple of days 
followed by a turn more westward. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Strengthening is forecast and Karina is likely to become a hurricane 
over the weekend. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 230 miles (370 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 999 mb (29.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Tropical Storm Karina will begin to
affect portions of the coast of southwest Mexico and the Baja
California Peninsula this weekend.  These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Tropical Storm Karina Forecast Discussion Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Fri Aug 28 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 280837
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Karina Discussion Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
200 AM MST Fri Aug 28 2026
 
Karina's structure on satellite imagery tonight is slowly evolving,
with a concentrated burst of deep convection with cloud top
temperatures below -80 C occurring near and to the east of the
center. However, scatterometer wind data around 05 UTC indicated
that the center was still on the edge of this convective burst, and
remains a bit elongated on its southwest end, where the cyclone is
interacting with the larger monsoon trough. The peak wind retrieval
was 41 kt, and that combined with little change in the subjective
or objective intensity estimates supports maintaining 45 kt for this
advisory.
 
The tropical storm is moving on a general northwest heading at 
310/11 kt. An established mid-level ridge over the southwestern U.S. 
should maintain this general motion over the next couple of days. 
Thereafter, this ridging begins to extend more zonally to the north 
of Karina, allowing the track of the cyclone to turn more westward 
in the 48-72 h time frame. Towards the end of the forecast period, 
guidance suggests this ridge will become eroded by a mid- to 
upper-level trough, which could result in Karina making a turn back 
to the northwest. The track guidance this morning has shifted a 
little south and west compared to the previous cycle, and the NHC 
forecast track has also been shifted in this direction, blending the 
latest HFIP Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA) and Google DeepMind 
(GDMI) aids.

Karina's wind field diagnosed by scatterometer earlier is still 
fairly broad, and it will likely take a bit more time for the 
cyclone to develop an inner core. However, environmental conditions 
beyond the next 24 h remain quite favorable for intensification, 
with low shear, warm waters, and a sufficiently moist deep-layer 
troposphere. SHIPS-RII guidance also continues to indicate elevated 
probabilities of rapid intensification that are 4-5 times the 
climatological mean. Thus, significant intensification is forecasted 
over the next 2-3 days, and the latest NHC intensity forecast is 
higher than the previous one, showing a 110 kt peak in about 72 h, 
though this forecast is still under some of the more aggressive 
guidance (HCCA, GDMI) but above some of the hurricane-regional model 
guidance this cycle (HAFS-A/B). In days 4-5 Karina should encounter 
a more stable environment as it approaches the northern edge of the 
26 C isotherm, and weakening is shown to begin by the end of the 
forecast period.

item.title: Tropical Storm Lowell Forecast Discussion Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Thu Aug 27 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 280835
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Lowell Discussion Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP122026
1100 PM HST Thu Aug 27 2026
 
Lowell continues to produce a persistent area of deep convection
on the southwest side of its circulation, and banding features are
gradually becoming better organized west of the center. The
latest satellite intensity estimates generally range from 35 to 45
kt, and based on those values, the initial wind speed is nudged up
to 40 kt for this advisory. The storm appears to be experiencing
some northeasterly vertical wind shear based on its convective
pattern.
 
The initial motion estimate remains east-northeastward, or 65 
degrees at 5 kt, and that general slow motion could continue through 
the day. However, a turn to the west or west-northwest with an 
increase in forward speed is expected on Saturday as a ridge 
strengthens to the north of the system. Although the models 
generally agree on this overall pattern evolution, there remains 
considerable spread in the location of the turn and forward speed of 
the storm after it turns westward. The NHC track forecast leans 
toward the faster side of the guidance envelope, but is not as fast 
as the Google DeepMind and HCCA solutions, which have had a slight 
fast bias on storms in the eastern and central Pacific so far this 
season.
 
Lowell is expected to be in generally favorable environmental 
conditions for the next several days, with warm sea-surface 
temperatures, light to moderate easterly wind shear and relatively 
moist air. However, strengthening could be slow in the short term 
given its asymmetric structure. Most of the more reliable models 
show at least steady strengthening throughout the forecast period, 
and it seems likely that Lowell will reach hurricane strength over 
the weekend with additional intensification continuing into early 
next week. The NHC intensity forecast is similiar to the previous 
one and lies near the high end of the guidance in the short term and 
closer to the middle of the envelope at the latter forecast times.
